name: Niger Delta Community-Driven Mangrove Restoration [Regular VPA 1]
description: The Niger Delta Community-Driven Mangrove Restoration Project is a scalable initiative focused on restoring the historically mangrove-rich wetlands of the Niger Delta through a community-led approach. The Niger Delta—the largest river delta in Africa and home to the world’s third-largest mangrove forest—has faced severe degradation over the past decades due to a variety of pressures. This has compromised biodiversity, diminished livelihoods, and increased vulnerability to flooding and erosion for the 30 million people who live there. This project aims to restore the ecosystem through training local communities to plant native, locally adapted mangrove species, while also addressing the causes of mangrove loss. Its objectives are to: • Empower communities by providing the livelihood support, education, and tools needed to become long-term ecosystem stewards and bolster their resilience in a climate-changing world, • Restore a critical ecosystem and its services while promoting biodiversity by rebuilding the habitats of numerous species, strengthening regional food security, and providing flood and storm protection. • And finally, sequester carbon in the fight against climate change while utilizing mangroves as a powerful nature-based solution. Rooted in strong local partnerships and ecosystem restoration approaches, the project is designed to scale and serve as a model for community-first restoration across Nigeria and the wider region.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: Niger Delta Community-Driven Mangrove Restoration Project

name: Empowering Communities Through Improved Cookstoves
description: The Empowering Communities Through Improved Cookstoves project in rural Togo distributes fuel-efficient improved cookstoves (ICS) to replace traditional, inefficient three-stone fires commonly used in rural households. The cookstoves are manufactured locally in Togo, supporting infrastructure development, generating employment, and stimulating economic growth in the region. By reducing the amount of firewood required for cooking, the project alleviates the time and physical burden of firewood collection—a task that disproportionately falls on women and girls. This, in turn, enables greater access to education and income-generating opportunities. In addition to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, the project delivers a range of co-benefits, including: Improved indoor air quality, reducing the incidence of respiratory and eye-related illnesses caused by smoke inhalation from traditional stoves. Reduced pressure on local forests through decreased firewood demand, slowing deforestation and preserving biodiversity. Lower household expenditure on cooking fuel due to more efficient wood use. Increased time savings for women and children, enabling greater focus on education, caregiving, and economic activities. Job creation and skill development through local cookstove production and distribution. By addressing both climate change and local development needs, the project contributes to eight Sustainable Development Goals.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: Resilient Futures: Building Resilience to Poverty and Climate Change

name: Resilient Futures: Building Resilience to Poverty and Climate Change
description:
The “Resilient Futures” Programme of Activities (PoA) is a community-driven initiative designed to address the interlinked challenges of poverty, environmental degradation, and climate change across vulnerable rural regions. By deploying scalable, high-impact interventions—such as improved cookstoves, safe water technologies, biochar production, and regenerative agroforestry—this PoA aims to reduce and remove greenhouse gas emissions while strengthening the adaptive capacity of local communities.

Led by trusted local partners and supported by ethical climate finance, the PoA empowers women, improves health outcomes, restores ecosystems, and increases household income and food security. 

This programme contributes to multiple Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 1 (No Poverty), SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being), SDG 5 (Gender Equality), SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 15 (Life on Land). 
The PoA is designed to enable the rapid scaling of ethical, verifiable carbon projects in West Africa and beyond—delivering measurable climate impact and real, lasting change for people and planet.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: GS12792 GS13130 VPA-2 Hygiene and Environmental Care for Tanks and Overhead Reservoirs (HECTOR)
description: Voluntary Project Activity 2 (VPA-2) under the HECTOR project represents a transformative initiative aimed at rural villages in the Anantapur District of Andhra Pradesh. This project is specifically designed to tackle the critical issues surrounding the availability of safe drinking water, aligning with the broader goals of India's Jal Jivan Mission. VPA-2 focuses on revolutionizing water purification by introducing advanced technologies, including automated chlorination units, UV disinfection systems, and real-time water quality monitoring powered by IoT and AI-ML. The strategic implementation of these solutions seeks to address the persistent challenges in rural areas, significantly improving water quality standards and enhancing access to safe drinking water for the communities involved.

name: GOKTEPE WPP Capacity Increase Project
description:
Erguvan Enerji Elektrik Üretim A.Ş. plans to launch the Göktepe Wind Power Plant Capacity Increase Project with a total installed capacity of 105.64 MWm / 105.64 MWe, based on the Electricity Generation License obtained from the Energy Market Regulatory Authority on 04/06/2020. The project will be implemented within the borders of Esenköy in Çınarcık District, and Mecidiye Village and Karşıyaka in Armutlu District, Yalova Province.
As part of the project, 19 wind turbines will be constructed and a Battery Energy Storage System will also be established. The electricity generated at the plant will be transmitted to the Yalova WPP and Yares Yalova WPP Transformer Substations via a 154 kV transmission line.
Scheduled to be commissioned in 2029, the Göktepe Wind Power Plant Capacity Increase Project is expected to supply approximately 260,625 MWh of electricity annually to the grid. Due to its renewable energy source, the wind power plant will also contribute to a reduction of approximately 165,366 tons of CO₂ equivalent emissions per year.

name: Landfill gas recovery, energy generation and  biogas distribution from CTR Santa Rosa
description:
1. Project Design and Scenarios
The project aims to collect and treat landfill gas (Landfill Gas – LFG) in various scenarios to reduce methane emissions. The planned scenarios include:
•Controlled flaring of collected gas;
•Supplying treated gas to industrial, commercial, or residential consumers;
•Using gas as fuel for electricity generation.
These scenarios will be applied according to the specific characteristics and needs of each landfill included in the program.
At the Santa Rosa Waste Treatment Center (CTR) in Seropédica (Rio de Janeiro – Brazil), the current scenario involves the capture of landfill gas (LFG) for combustion and distribution to external consumers. In the future, infrastructure is planned for electricity generation from the collected gas.
2. Technologies and Measures
The project uses modern technologies for LFG capture, treatment, and utilization, such as:
•Vertical and horizontal wells for gas collection;
•High-efficiency flaring systems;
•Infrastructure for gas treatment, including contaminant removal;
•Infrastructure for transporting biogas by trucks for external thermal applications.
For future phases, CTR Santa Rosa also plans to install modular equipment for electricity generation.
Additionally, the project includes strict monitoring to ensure operational efficiency and safety.
3. Geographic Boundaries
Currently, the project only includes CTR Santa Rosa in Seropédica/RJ. Geographic coordinates: -22.795703 (latitude) and -43.760558 (longitude).
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
project_developer: CICLUS AMBIENTAL DO BRASIL S A

name: Nicaragua Sun Power
description:
The Sun Power Project is a 30 MW (AC) photovoltaic solar plant located in the municipality of Nagarote, within the department of León, Nicaragua. This facility will comprise 62,070 solar modules, achieving a total installed capacity of 38 MWp and a net capacity of 30 MW. 
The primary objective of this project is to contribute to the development of Nicaragua's electricity sector while adhering to sustainability principles and fostering the transformation of the country's energy matrix towards renewable and clean energy sources. The solar park aims to comply with international climate change mitigation standards, aligning with worldwide efforts to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and promote a more sustainable future.
In conclusion, the SunPower Project is not only designed to enhance Nicaragua’s energy supply but also plays a pivotal role in supporting the country's commitments to environmental sustainability and facilitating the transition to a cleaner, more responsible energy matrix.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: ATEC Biodigesters in Bangladesh
description: The ATEC Biodigesters in Bangladesh project is designed to serve rural households that primarily rely on fi rewood and biomass fuels for cooking. The primary target group consists of small-scale farming households that own 3 to 5 cows, as they can eff ectively utilize biogas technology to meet their cooking needs. This initiative aims to tackle the pressing challenges of clean cooking, environmental degradation, and rural household energy dependence by providing sustainable cooking solutions for low-income households. By introducing ATEC’s biodigesters and biogas stoves, this project will replace traditional firewood stoves with highly efficient and eco-friendly alternatives. Beyond environmental benefits, the project is designed to improve the well-being of household members, particularly women, infants, and children. By reducing exposure to indoor air pollution, it helps lower the risk of respiratory illnesses and related health expenses. Additionally, it alleviates the burden of fi rewood collection, freeing up valuable time for education, economic activities, and improved quality of life.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: GS12953 GS12954 RVPA-2 Pungue Project
description: Mozambique is classified as a Least Developed Country by the United Nations, and only half of Mozambicans have access to improved water supply in rural areas. Handpumps, which are commonly found in communities, often fall into disrepair shortly after installation due to insufficient maintenance, lack of access to spare parts, and financial support. The Pungue project, developed by Removall, aims to rehabilitate and sustain handpumps across Sofala province of Mozambique. It will avoid the consumption of firewood by households and lead to a reduction of carbon dioxide emissions.

name: Healthy Kitchens and Happy Lives in Tanzania-VPA01
description:
The project will disseminate improved cook stoves (ICS) – to households within Tanzania. By providing clean cooking, the project will ensure that households consume less firewood during the process of cooking and as a result there shall be a reduction of carbon dioxide emissions from the combustion process. 
Most people in Sub-Saharan Africa rely on gathering biomass for cooking, in particular in rural areas, which dramatically damages health and impairs productivity improvements. The procurement and consumption of these fuels define the character of everyday life in many developing countries.
In line to its vision of delivering high impact related to health, savings and convenience, SDG 13 Ventures Pte. Ltd. is undertaking an extensive distribution programme to create a nation-wide access of Clean Cookstoves for low-income consumer.
The project will contribute in achieving SDGs including, SDG-01: 1 No poverty, SDG-3: Good Health and Well Being, SDG-5: Gender Equality, SDG 7- Affordable and Clean energy, SDG 8: Full and productive employment and decent work for all, SDG 10 Reduced Inequalities and SDG-13: Climate Action. The programme would result in GHG emission reductions and other impact outcomes which can be traded internationally and the revenue collected from such trade will benefit the scaling up of the project and thereby assist other households who are still using traditional stoves.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: Healthy Kitchens and Happy Lives in Africa
